key_insight: A penalization-based deep backward scheme approximates reflected BSDEs with a proven value-process mean-square error of O(|π|^{1/3}) after balancing dominant errors.
engineering_relevance: The scheme offers a theoretically controlled neural approach to constrained stochastic models, including American option valuation.
method: Replace reflection with penalized BSDEs and approximate backward in time using neural networks.
Use monotonicity to establish stability and spatial Lipschitz bounds uniform in the penalty parameter.
Separate penalization, time-discretization, forward, and neural approximation errors.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports quantitative error estimates for Y and Z, plus numerical experiments on an explicit reflected BSDE and American options in one-dimensional and structured high-dimensional settings.
watch_item: The analysis assumes a generator independent of the control variable Z, limiting direct applicability to more general reflected BSDEs.
paper_title: A Deep Backward Scheme for Reflected BSDEs via Penalization : Approximation and Convergence Analysis
